summary: A consultant-level look at the stewardship decisions that now have trial evidence. Procalcitonin-guided stopping (PRORATA, SAPS, and the UK ADAPT-Sepsis trial, JAMA 2025) safely shortens courses, but only by about a day, and CRP-guided stopping showed no benefit. Shorter fixed courses are supported by BALANCE (NEJM 2025: 7 vs 14 days for bloodstream infection, excluding S. aureus and severe immunosuppression) and, for VAP, by Chastre (2003) and REGARD-VAP (2024), with residual uncertainty for non-fermenting Gram-negatives and Pseudomonas. BLING III (JAMA 2024) narrowly missed its mortality endpoint for continuous beta-lactam infusion, but the accompanying meta-analysis favoured prolonged infusion, and the Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2026 guideline now recommends it strongly after a loading dose. Beta-lactam TDM (TARGET, DOLPHIN) improves target attainment but has not improved outcomes. The only de-escalation RCT (Leone 2014) was small and unfavourable. The UK INHALE trial of a multiplex PCR pneumonia panel improved early prescribing but failed to show non-inferior clinical cure. On guidance: NICE NG253 (Nov 2025) has a procalcitonin update in progress, UKHSA's Start Smart Then Focus (2023) sets the 48-72 hour CARES review, an ESICM-endorsed 2020 position paper supports routine beta-lactam TDM, and SSC 2026 makes conditional recommendations for procalcitonin-guided stopping, shorter courses, TDM and rapid diagnostics.
takeaways: For uncomplicated Gram-negative bacteraemia with source control, seven days is the default; BALANCE supports it (it excluded S. aureus and severe immunosuppression).
Procalcitonin-guided stopping is safe but saves only about a day (ADAPT-Sepsis); CRP-guided stopping has no trial support.
Give piperacillin-tazobactam and meropenem as prolonged or continuous infusions, always after a loading dose (BLING III, the 2024 meta-analysis, SSC 2026 strong recommendation).
For VAP, stop once the patient has been stable for 48 hours, often by day seven or earlier (REGARD-VAP); take more care with non-fermenting Gram-negatives.
Beta-lactam TDM and rapid multiplex PCR improve process measures but have not yet improved outcomes (TARGET, DOLPHIN, INHALE); use them case by case.
